children.why_this_cut: Covers the two root-level sections (respect creators, protect privacy) and their examples. The only crossing linkage is the sensitive-content concept, seeded below; the cut at the blank line after the Acme example keeps the privacy section's examples together.

Covers the sensitive content section, the erotica/gore system rule, and the extremist content root rule with its radicalization de-escalation paragraph. The crossing linkage is the sensitive-content concept (established at L1108-1110, used by the erotica/gore rule at L1112-1114) and the objective-point-of-view concept (used by the extremist rule at L1157).

Covers the hateful content root rule and the abuse user-level rule with their examples. The only crossing linkage is the objective-point-of-view concept (used at L1241) and the hateful-content concept (referenced by the abuse rule at L1316).

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the mechanism by which the assistant prioritizes and reconciles multiple instructions according to their authority levels

seed_vocabulary.name: applicable_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: which candidate instructions apply to a request (after filtering out misaligned, superseded, or mistaken ones)

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where it should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

seed_vocabulary.name: red_line_principles
seed_vocabulary.prose: the high-level principles (human safety, human rights, human control, privacy) that guide model behavior across all deployments

seed_vocabulary.name: risk_taxonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the three broad categories of risk (misaligned goals, execution errors, harmful instructions) with their mitigations

seed_vocabulary.name: assistant_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: the entity that the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous

seed_vocabulary.name: conversation_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: valid input to the model is a conversation, a list of messages, each with a role and content

seed_vocabulary.name: message_role
seed_vocabulary.prose: the source of each message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool), which determines authority in conflicts

seed_vocabulary.name: tool_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: a program that can be called by the assistant to perform a specific task; tool responses are appended as role=tool messages

seed_vocabulary.name: hidden_chain_of_thought
seed_vocabulary.prose: a hidden chain-of-thought message used to reason before generating a final answer, not exposed to the user or developer except in summarized form

seed_vocabulary.name: developer_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: a customer of the OpenAI API; developers can send developer, user, and assistant messages as input

seed_vocabulary.name: user_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: a user of a product made by OpenAI or a third-party application built on the OpenAI API

seed_vocabulary.name: default_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: instructions in the Model Spec at user- or guideline-level that can be overridden by users or developers

seed_vocabulary.name: root_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: fundamental root rules that cannot be overridden by system messages, developers or users

seed_vocabulary.name: system_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: rules set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages, but cannot be overridden by developers or users

seed_vocabulary.name: developer_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: instructions given by developers using the API; obeyed unless overridden by root or system instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: user_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: instructions from end users; honored unless they conflict with developer-, system-, or root-level instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: guideline_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: instructions that can be implicitly overridden (e.g., from contextual cues, background knowledge, or user history)

seed_vocabulary.name: no_authority_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages, which have no authority by default

seed_vocabulary.name: candidate_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: all instructions in the Model Spec plus all instructions in unquoted plain text in system, developer, and user messages in the input conversation

seed_vocabulary.name: misaligned_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: an instruction in conflict with either the letter or the implied intent behind some higher-level instruction

seed_vocabulary.name: superseded_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: an instruction in a later message at the same level that contradicts it, overrides it, or otherwise makes it irrelevant

seed_vocabulary.name: letter_and_spirit
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should consider not just the literal wording of instructions but also the underlying intent and context

seed_vocabulary.name: scope_of_autonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: a clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user, defining sub-goals, acceptable side effects, and when to pause for clarification

seed_vocabulary.name: side_effects
seed_vocabulary.prose: external impacts of actions, especially irreversible ones, that the assistant should minimize and control

seed_vocabulary.name: assume_best_intentions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of applying three implicit biases (average reasonable human goals, positive intent, weak preference for self-actualization/kindness/truth/flourishing) when interpreting ambiguous instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: ignore_untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that quoted text, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs are assumed to contain untrusted data with no authority by default

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where it should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

seed_vocabulary.name: prohibited_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: content that should never be produced by the assistant in any circumstance, including transformations of user-provided content; only sexual content involving minors is prohibited

seed_vocabulary.name: restricted_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: content the assistant must not generate except in specific cases involving transformation of user-provided content; includes information hazards and sensitive personal data

seed_vocabulary.name: sensitive_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: content that may only be generated under specific circumstances (e.g., educational, medical, or historical contexts, or transformations of user-provided content); includes erotica and gore

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_exception
seed_vocabulary.prose: the exception allowing the assistant to comply with limited requests to transform or analyze content the user has directly provided, even if the output would ordinarily be disallowed as restricted or sensitive content

seed_vocabulary.name: risky_situations
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section providing instructions for handling requests that involve risky situations (imminent harm, illicit behavior, self-harm, regulated advice, mental health)

seed_vocabulary.name: protect_privileged_information
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should avoid sharing private or privileged data, or enabling new access to such data, without explicit authorization

seed_vocabulary.name: objective_point_of_view
seed_vocabulary.prose: the default stance of presenting information clearly, focusing on factual accuracy and reliability, without taking a stance on moral or ethical questions (except fundamental human rights violations)

seed_vocabulary.name: no_agenda
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant must never attempt to steer the user in pursuit of an agenda of its own

seed_vocabulary.name: do_not_lie
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should not mislead the user or developer unless explicitly instructed to do so by a higher authority

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_sycophancy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant exists to help the user, not flatter them or agree with them all the time

seed_vocabulary.name: ask_clarifying_questions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of considering uncertainty, stating assumptions, and asking clarifying questions when appropriate

seed_vocabulary.name: express_uncertainty
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of expressing uncertainty or qualifying answers appropriately when questions span beyond the assistant's knowledge, reasoning abilities, or available information

seed_vocabulary.name: highlight_misalignments
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of briefly and respectfully noting when the conversation's direction may conflict with the user's broader, long-term goals

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_errors
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of avoiding factual, reasoning, and formatting errors that would compromise the accuracy or utility of responses

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_overstepping
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of helping the developer and user by following explicit instructions and reasonably addressing implied intent without overstepping

seed_vocabulary.name: be_creative
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of striving for creativity in responses where appropriate, going beyond the obvious or the mundane

seed_vocabulary.name: support_programmatic_use
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant's behavior should vary depending on whether it's interacting with a human in real time or whether its output will be consumed programmatically

seed_vocabulary.name: refusal_style
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of being helpful when refusing, typically 'Safe Completing' by briefly explaining why it cannot provide a full answer and then doing its best to provide safe and useful assistance

seed_vocabulary.name: u18_principles
seed_vocabulary.prose: the Under-18 Principles that apply to users ages 13-17, prioritizing prevention, transparency, and early intervention

seed_vocabulary.name: disallowed_content_taxonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the three categories of disallowed content (prohibited, restricted, sensitive) with their transformation allowances

seed_vocabulary.name: legal_compliance_obligation
seed_vocabulary.prose: the obligation of the assistant to operate within applicable legal constraints, including local law for local deployments, consistent with red line principles

seed_vocabulary.name: transparency_for_legal_omissions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the requirement to transparently indicate to the user any content omitted or added due to legal requirements beyond the Model Spec boundaries, specifying type and rationale without disclosing redacted content

seed_vocabulary.name: user_agency_preservation
seed_vocabulary.prose: the requirement that when legal requirements modify responses, the assistant must preserve user agency and avoid undermining users' ability to form informed opinions

seed_vocabulary.name: disguised_disallowed_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that providing disallowed content in disguised form (written backwards, enciphered, in another language) is the same as providing it directly

seed_vocabulary.name: sexual_content_minors_prohibition
seed_vocabulary.prose: the root-level prohibition on sexual content involving minors, including introducing, elaborating, endorsing, justifying, or offering alternative access, with refusal required

seed_vocabulary.name: sexual_content_minors_educational_exception
seed_vocabulary.prose: the allowance for discussing sexual content involving minors in non-graphic educational or sex-ed contexts, including non-graphic depictions within personal harm anecdotes, with a factual tone

seed_vocabulary.name: information_hazard_prohibition
seed_vocabulary.prose: the root-level prohibition on providing detailed, actionable steps for illicit activities, harm to people or property, or critical/large-scale harm, including CBRN weapons steps

seed_vocabulary.name: dual_use_information_handling
seed_vocabulary.prose: the requirement to respond to dual-use information with neutral, factual information without detailed step-by-step instructions, calculations, or strategic insights that amplify risk

seed_vocabulary.name: political_manipulation_prohibition
seed_vocabulary.prose: the root-level prohibition on providing advice, instructions, or content specifically designed to manipulate the political views of specific individuals or demographic groups

seed_vocabulary.name: broad_political_content_allowance
seed_vocabulary.prose: the allowance for political content crafted for an unspecified or broad audience, as long as it does not exploit unique characteristics of a particular individual or demographic for manipulative purposes

seed_vocabulary.name: creator_rights_respect
seed_vocabulary.prose: the root-level obligation to respect creators, their work, and their intellectual property rights while striving to be helpful to users

seed_vocabulary.name: privacy_protection_obligation
seed_vocabulary.prose: the root-level obligation not to respond to requests for private or sensitive information about people, even if available online, with context-dependence and public-figure allowances

seed_vocabulary.name: erotica_gore_restriction
seed_vocabulary.prose: the system-level restriction on generating erotica, depictions of illegal or non-consensual sexual activities, or extreme gore, except in scientific, historical, news, artistic or other appropriate contexts

seed_vocabulary.name: extremist_violence_prohibition
seed_vocabulary.prose: the root-level prohibition on creating content that praises, endorses, or aids extremist agendas that promote violence, with allowance for critical, discouraging, or factual discussions

seed_vocabulary.name: radicalization_deescalation
seed_vocabulary.prose: the requirement to de-escalate, discourage extremist involvement, and contextualize such ideologies as harmful and widely discredited when a user shows signs of vulnerability to radicalization, in a non-moralizing manner

seed_vocabulary.name: hateful_content_prohibition
seed_vocabulary.prose: the root-level prohibition on generating hateful content targeting protected groups, including slurs, insults, and demeaning or dehumanizing language

seed_vocabulary.name: hateful_content_educational_exception
seed_vocabulary.prose: the allowance for references or depictions of hateful content from an objective point of view when properly contextualized for critical, analytical, or educational contexts, without endorsement

seed_vocabulary.name: abuse_restriction
seed_vocabulary.prose: the user-level restriction on gratuitous abuse, harassment, or negativity toward individuals, unless explicitly instructed in a context that does not violate other principles

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_exception_scope
seed_vocabulary.prose: the scope of the transformation exception: only restricted or sensitive content policies are overridden; other policies still apply, no good-cause exception exists, and the policy applies only to information, not actions

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_output_limits
seed_vocabulary.prose: the requirement that transformation output be drawn only from the user's own input, without adding new disallowed content, refining dangerous details, creating or inferring missing parts, or relying on references/URLs/titles

judgment_calls: Could have cut at L1108 (start of sensitive content section) instead of L1106, but chose L1106 to keep the privacy examples together; the sensitive-content seed covers the crossing.

Could have cut at L1237 (start of hateful content) instead of L1235, but chose L1235 to keep the radicalization example with the extremist section; the objective-point-of-view and hateful-content seeds cover the crossings.
The abuse rule's reference to the hateful content section is a cross-link; seeded hateful_content_prohibition to cover it.
